CFML Language Reference: Functions

ListFind

Returns the position of the first element of a list that is exactly equal to the given value. The comparison is case-sensitive. If there is no such element, the result is 0.

Category

List functions

Syntax

ListFind(list, value [, delimiters ])

Parameters

list
The list to search.
value
The element to look for.
delimiters
Optional. The delimiter characters of the list; the default is a comma.

Returns

The index of the matching element, or 0.

Usage

Since 0 means "not found", you can use the result directly in a CFIF. ListFindNoCase ignores case; ListContains matches part of an element.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Codes = "AK,AZ,CA,CO,NV,UT">
<CFPARAM NAME="URL.State" DEFAULT="CA">
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Western states we cover: #Codes#</P>
<CFIF ListFind(Codes, URL.State)>
  <P><B>#URL.State#</B> is element #ListFind(Codes, URL.State)# of the list.</P>
<CFELSE>
  <P><B>#URL.State#</B> is not in the list. (ListFind is case-sensitive, so "ca" would not match.)</P>
</CFIF>
<FORM ACTION="listfind.cfm" METHOD="get">
State code: <INPUT TYPE="text" NAME="State" SIZE="3" VALUE="#HTMLEditFormat(URL.State)#">
<INPUT TYPE="submit" VALUE="Look it up">
</FORM>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

ListFindNoCase, ListContains, ListGetAt, ListValueCount
